title: Free ChatGPT has ads now. Here is what switching them off costs you. (off day, approved by Krish 17 Nov)
experiment: Sensational covers and designed body type: the cover is a man in pyjamas recoiling from a chat assistant smothered in sponsored links, salesmen reaching out of the screen; each body card has a mono kicker, a mint rule and Archivo Black with the key phrase in mint.

five_whys.q: Why does a free ChatGPT user care?
five_whys.a: Free ChatGPT now shows sponsored cards under some answers in the countries where OpenAI runs ads.

five_whys.q: Why are there ads at all?
five_whys.a: Most people use the free plan, and running it costs OpenAI a fortune, so ads pay for it.

five_whys.q: Why don't people switch them off?
five_whys.a: The off switch is buried in settings and nobody has said what it costs you.

five_whys.q: Why is the trade-off wider than ChatGPT?
five_whys.a: Free AI is following free search and social media: you pay with attention unless you pay with money or features.

five_whys.q: Why should a business person act this week?
five_whys.a: Staff on free plans see ads beside work answers; a team should choose its plan on purpose, not by default.

explains.temporary chat: a chat ChatGPT forgets as soon as you close it (card 5)

cards.source: Krish's research doc 'When the Assistant Becomes the Ad' (5 Nov 2026): the average US user already yields about $1,000 a year to Meta, Google and Amazon; ChatGPT ads at a ~$1B run-rate (31 Aug 2026)

cards.headline: A temporary chat in ChatGPT shows no ads, but forgets the whole conversation when you close it.
cards.picture: The trade-off scale: no ads on one side, no memory on the other

cards.headline: The ads switch in ChatGPT's settings removes ads, but then the free plan allows fewer messages and no images.

cards.headline: Paying for ChatGPT Plus removes the ads, and staying free means living with ads, forgotten chats or fewer messages.
cards.picture: The trade-off scale balanced, the house robot shrugging
